is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles arabiensis and Anopheles gambiae (s.s.) in Kisumu County, Kenya (Title, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study screened for mutations at Vgsc-1014F, Vgsc-1014S, Vgsc-1575Y, and Ace1-119S (Abstract, Page 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides allele frequencies for L1014F and L1014S along with the number of mosquitoes genotyped (N) for each species and ecological zone.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from field sites in Kisumu County, Kenya, in 2022–2023 (Abstract, Page 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting original empirical data on insecticide resistance and target-site mutations.

sub_country_location.evidence: Thirteen specific sites were surveyed in Kisumu County, including Nyalenda, Gesoko, Migosi, Mamboleo, Bandani, Kotetni, Kandalo, Tiengre, Kisian, Ojola, Mainga, Chulaimbo, and Marera (Page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected and tested between August 2022 and December 2023 (Page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes routine field collections supported by NIH grants (R01 AI123074, etc.) and does not indicate that the data is a subset of a larger previously published dataset.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequency and sample size data are provided in Table 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study investigated insecticide resistance levels and underlying mechanisms in Anopheles arabiensis and Anopheles gambiae across an urban-to-rural continuum in Kisumu County, Kenya. Field-collected larvae from 2022-2023 were reared to adults and tested using WHO bioassays. Genotyping for Vgsc (L1014F, L1014S, N1575Y) and Ace-1 (G119S) mutations was performed on 1,067 mosquitoes, with allele frequencies reported by species and ecological zone. High pyrethroid resistance and elevated L1014F frequencies were observed in urban An. arabiensis populations.
